Use this document as the starting point for the project. Open
`IFLS_Project.Rproj`, then open this file and click **Knit**. You can also run
the chunks in order in RStudio while the project is open.

This document calls the existing R scripts, prepares folders, checks packages,
and lists the original Stata files. CSV conversion is controlled by a setting
below. The original datasets are never cleaned, filtered, merged, or overwritten.

If **Knit** is unavailable because R Markdown is not installed, run this once in
the RStudio Console before knitting:

```{r first-time-rmarkdown, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "knitr"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

# Choose the project location and settings

The path below is your current project folder. Keep this master file directly
inside that folder, alongside `IFLS_Project.Rproj` and `config.R`.

For the first run, keep `convert_dta_to_csv <- FALSE` to inspect the setup. Once
your source files are in place, change it to `TRUE` and knit again to create CSVs.
The converter's overwrite setting remains in `config.R` and defaults to `FALSE`.

```{r settings, error=FALSE}
# 1. Your actual local project folder
project_folder <- paste0(
  "/Users/khaira_abdillah/Documents/IFLS_Causal_Project/",
  "IFLS-Socio-Economic-Data-Analysis-Project-main"
)

# 2. Which steps should run?
install_missing_packages <- TRUE
run_converter_check <- TRUE
convert_dta_to_csv <- FALSE

# 3. Check the project folder before continuing
if (!dir.exists(project_folder)) {
  stop("Project folder was not found. Edit project_folder in the settings chunk.")
}

project_folder <- normalizePath(project_folder, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

if (!file.exists(file.path(project_folder, "IFLS_Project.Rproj"))) {
  stop("IFLS_Project.Rproj was not found inside the selected project folder.")
}

# 4. Use this folder for all following chunks during knitting
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_folder)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  cache = FALSE,
  error = FALSE,
  message = TRUE,
  warning = TRUE
)

cat("Project folder:", project_folder, "\n")
```

# Check that the existing scripts are available

This master document reuses the scripts already in your project. Run it from the
project root so that their relative paths work consistently.

```{r check-project-files}
if (normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE) != project_folder) {
  stop("Open the correct IFLS_Project.Rproj before running the chunks manually.")
}

required_files <- c(
  "config.R",
  "02_scripts/00_setup_folders.R",
  "02_scripts/01_install_packages.R",
  "02_scripts/02a_convert_one_dta.R",
  "02_scripts/02_convert_all_dta_to_csv.R",
  "02_scripts/checks/check_conversion.R"
)

missing_files <- required_files[
  !file.exists(file.path(project_folder, required_files))
]

if (length(missing_files) > 0L) {
  stop("Required project files are missing: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

cat("All required project scripts were found.\n")
```

# Install and check packages

With `install_missing_packages <- TRUE`, the existing installation script installs
only packages that are missing. Installed packages are not reinstalled or upgraded.
Package installation needs an internet connection.

```{r packages}
if (install_missing_packages) {
  source("02_scripts/01_install_packages.R", local = TRUE)
}

packages_needed <- c("haven", "readr", "rmarkdown", "knitr")
packages_available <- vapply(
  packages_needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE
)

if (any(!packages_available)) {
  stop(
    "Required packages are missing: ",
    paste(packages_needed[!packages_available], collapse = ", "),
    ". Set install_missing_packages <- TRUE and run again."
  )
}

package_table <- data.frame(
  package = packages_needed,
  version = vapply(
    packages_needed,
    function(package) as.character(utils::packageVersion(package)),
    character(1)
  )
)

knitr::kable(package_table, caption = "Packages available for this setup")
```

# Create the folders and load the project paths

This step can be repeated. Existing files stay in place. The script also loads
`config.R`, which defines the data and documentation paths used below.

```{r prepare-folders}
source("02_scripts/00_setup_folders.R", local = TRUE)

folder_table <- data.frame(
  purpose = c(
    "Documentation", "Original Stata data", "CSV copies", "Metadata",
    "Intermediate datasets", "Analysis datasets", "Run logs"
  ),
  folder = c(
    documentation_folder, raw_dta_folder, raw_csv_folder, metadata_folder,
    intermediate_folder, analysis_folder, logs_folder
  )
)

folder_table$exists <- dir.exists(folder_table$folder)
if (!all(folder_table$exists)) {
  stop("Some project folders could not be created. Check folder permissions.")
}

knitr::kable(folder_table, caption = "Project folders")
```

# Put the source files in place

Use these paths relative to the project folder. Keep downloaded source filenames
and extracted subfolders such as `hh07_all_dta`.

| Content | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| IFLS4 household Stata datasets | `01_data/01_raw_dta/ifls4/household/hh07_all_dta/` |
| IFLS4 community Stata datasets | `01_data/01_raw_dta/ifls4/community/` |
| IFLS5 household Stata datasets | `01_data/01_raw_dta/ifls5/household/` |
| IFLS5 community Stata datasets | `01_data/01_raw_dta/ifls5/community/` |
| IFLS4 questionnaires | `00_documentation/ifls4/questionnaires/` |
| IFLS4 codebooks | `00_documentation/ifls4/codebooks/` |
| IFLS4 user guides | `00_documentation/ifls4/user_guides/` |

Use the same pattern for the other surveys. You can start with one survey;
the other survey folders can remain empty. Extract `.zip` archives before running
the converter, which reads `.dta` files rather than archives.

Your known IFLS4 source file is checked here. Its absence does not stop setup if
you are preparing the project before copying data.

```{r check-known-source}
example_source <- file.path(
  raw_dta_folder, "ifls4", "household", "hh07_all_dta", "b1_cov.dta"
)

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  file = example_source,
  found = file.exists(example_source)
), caption = "Check your existing IFLS4 file")
```

# Create an inventory of all original Stata files

This step lists files recursively, including nested folders. It does not load
the datasets into memory. The full inventory is saved in
`05_outputs/logs/source_file_inventory.csv`; this report displays up to 30 files.

```{r source-inventory}
source_files <- sort(list.files(
  raw_dta_folder,
  pattern = "\\.dta$",
  ignore.case = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
))

relative_files <- substring(source_files, nchar(raw_dta_folder) + 2L)

source_inventory <- data.frame(
  source_file = relative_files,
  size_mb = round(file.info(source_files)$size / 1024^2, 2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

readr::write_csv(
  source_inventory,
  file.path(logs_folder, "source_file_inventory.csv"),
  na = ""
)

cat("Original Stata files found:", nrow(source_inventory), "\n\n")

if (nrow(source_inventory) > 0L) {
  knitr::kable(
    head(source_inventory, 30),
    caption = "Original source files: first 30 entries"
  )
} else {
  cat("Copy your extracted .dta files into 01_data/01_raw_dta, then run again.")
}
```

# Check the converter using synthetic data

The check uses temporary example data to test labels, tagged missing values,
leading-zero identifiers, dates, nested folders, repeated runs, and changed
sources. It does not read or alter your IFLS files. A failed check stops this
document before the full conversion.

```{r converter-check}
if (run_converter_check) {
  source("02_scripts/checks/check_conversion.R", local = TRUE)
} else {
  cat("Synthetic converter check was skipped by your settings.\n")
}
```

# Create the CSV copies

Change `convert_dta_to_csv <- TRUE` in the first settings chunk when ready,
then knit this document again or rerun the chunks in order.

The conversion mirrors the original subfolders. For your IFLS4 example:

| Output | Relative path |
| --- | --- |
| Original Stata file | `01_data/01_raw_dta/ifls4/household/hh07_all_dta/b1_cov.dta` |
| Generated CSV | `01_data/02_raw_csv/ifls4/household/hh07_all_dta/b1_cov.csv` |
| Companion metadata folder | `01_data/03_metadata/ifls4/household/hh07_all_dta/` |

The CSV keeps the response codes. Companion metadata files hold variable labels,
value labels, and tagged missing-value positions. Keep the original `.dta` files
as the authoritative source; CSV does not retain every Stata feature.

```{r convert-data}
conversion_completed <- FALSE

if (convert_dta_to_csv) {
  if (length(source_files) == 0L) {
    stop("Conversion was requested, but no source .dta files were found.")
  }

  source("02_scripts/02_convert_all_dta_to_csv.R", local = TRUE)
  conversion_completed <- TRUE
} else {
  cat("Setup completed without running the full data conversion.\n")
  cat("Set convert_dta_to_csv <- TRUE to create the CSV copies.\n")
}
```

```{r conversion-results}
if (conversion_completed) {
  status_counts <- as.data.frame(table(conversion_inventory$status))
  names(status_counts) <- c("status", "files")

  cat("\nDetailed conversion inventory:", inventory_file, "\n")
  knitr::kable(status_counts, caption = "Results of this conversion run")
}
```

# Review what is ready

```{r setup-summary}
csv_files <- list.files(
  raw_csv_folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", ignore.case = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
)

setup_summary <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "Original Stata files found",
    "CSV files currently present",
    "Synthetic check requested",
    "Full conversion requested",
    "Full conversion completed in this run"
  ),
  value = c(
    as.character(length(source_files)), as.character(length(csv_files)),
    as.character(run_converter_check), as.character(convert_dta_to_csv),
    as.character(conversion_completed)
  )
)

knitr::kable(setup_summary, caption = "Setup summary")
```

The CSV file count includes exports from earlier runs. It is not, by itself,
proof that every source file has a current export. When conversion runs, use its
status inventory to check the results. Generated data, metadata, documentation
downloads, and logs stay local under the repository's existing exclusion rules.

After setup, we can explore the source datasets and construct the education
analysis sample in separate scripts and notebooks.

```{r session-information}
session_information <- capture.output(sessionInfo())
writeLines(session_information, file.path(logs_folder, "master_setup_session.txt"))
cat(session_information, sep = "\n")
```
